text:
The Devils made the trade of the fall on Oct. 23, sending Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Nick Bjugstad, prospect Alexander Command and two picks to Winnipeg for Connor Hellebuyck. He had asked out of Winnipeg and said this week threats against his family were behind it. Coach Sheldon Keefe and GM Sunny Mehta then kept him out of Tuesday's return there, citing win probability; Mercer scored twice and the Jets won.

That one night aside, the Devils are 14-6-0 and the process is excellent. They own 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), among the best shares we track. The one leak all season was in net: they have allowed about five more goals than their chances predicted, exactly the hole Hellebuyck was brought in to fill. He won all five of his starts before the Winnipeg trip.

Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored opponents 12-4 together, Hughes was the NHL's second star of the week, and Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes are plus-10 in goals as a pair. They also stay out of the box (2.65 minors a game, 3.85 drawn). Anthony Mantha going to long-term injured reserve thins the depth, and Lenni Hämeenaho's goal in Thursday's 5-2 win over Washington is the kind of audition that matters now. Our numbers give them a 95% chance at the playoffs and a projection near 107 points.
headline: Hellebuyck arrives, and the Devils already looked the part
